Could Syria become the focus of an Israeli-Turkish conflict?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:14:00 UTC
22:14:00 KST

Could Syria become the focus of an Israeli-Turkish conflict?
August 26, 2026
Following US mediation, Syrian and Israeli representatives met in Jordan last weekend for the first time in months. The talks aimed to defuse tensions following the recent Israeli attacks on Syrian territory and prevent hostilities between Israel and Turkey from spilling over into Syria.
The escalation was sparked by an Israeli attack on the Abu Duhur military airfield in Idlib Province on August 18. According to Syrian sources, the attack struck the runway and storage facilities without causing any fatalities. Israel stated that Syria had violated — or threatened to violate — a previous security agreement by allowing Turkish troops to use the airfield. Damascus and Ankara rejected these allegations.
The US criticized the attack by its Israeli ally as an "unnecessary escalation." In diplomatic terms, this amounts to a fairly clear show of rhetorical support for Ankara and Damascus.
Israel views a potential Turkish military presence in Syria as a red line. Yet, it remains unclear whether such a deployment is planned in the long term or whether it was even imminent at the time of the attack. Evidence on this matter is not publicly available.
However, as early as April 2025, Reuters news agency cited anonymous sources saying Turkey had inspected at least three air bases in Syria where it might want to station troops as part of a planned joint defense pact. Israeli airstrikes were already taking place at that time as well.
The Washington-based think tank Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), which is considered pro-Israel, justifies the attack as follows: "Israel worries that Ankara could eventually use its military presence in Syria as a platform to pressure or threaten Israel, and remains wary of the close relationship between Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa and the Turkish leadership."
Syria, Turkey and Israel disagree on the future order
For Bente Scheller, Syria expert at the German Green Party-affiliated Heinrich Böll Foundation, this explanation falls short.
"There is no evidence so far that Turkish troops are actually supposed to be stationed there," she told DW. While Israel may indeed have its own intelligence, the recent attack must be viewed against the backdrop of Israel's overall policy toward Syria as well as Turkey's growing regional role, she noted.
Marcus Schneider, a Middle East analyst at Germany's Friedrich Ebert Foundation — which is affiliated with the German Social Democratic Party (SPD) — in Beirut, also points out that a struggle for power and influence is unfolding in Syria and beyond.
"The attack primarily raises the question of what kind of military order will emerge in Syria in the future," he told DW. In his view, Israel wants to keep Syria weak, as a sovereign state that controls its own airspace would restrict Israel's military freedom of action. "The corridor for attacks against Iran runs through Syria," explained Schneider. A sovereign Syria could therefore pose a strategic obstacle to Israel.
Following the Hamas terror attacks on Israel on October 7, Israel's heightened security concerns are understandable, adds Scheller. In addition, Israel is certainly viewing with concern another development that extends beyond Syria.
"Israel is undoubtedly aware of how Turkey is currently attempting to position itself as a regional hegemon," Scheller said. The attack on Abu al-Duhur is therefore "clearly also a message to Turkey."
Turkey supports Syrian President al-Sharaa and is committed to a unified Syria which includes the territory in the country's northeast, where the majority of Syria's Kurdish population is located. For years, Turkey has been attacking the former Kurdish-led autonomous zone along its southern border. On Tuesday, the commander of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced the official dissolution of the group.
An analysis by the US think tank Carnegie Foundation describes the situation as a strategic rivalry between Israel and Turkey: "The northeast is also the main arena where two externally-driven strategic visions for Syria collide." The International Crisis Group also views Syria as a fault line between Turkey, a rising regional power, and Israel.
Syria's closer relations with the US
Syria's improved relations with the US — which amount to US support — offer new prospects for the country, despite the Islamist past of its new leader, President Ahmad al-Sharaa. In summer 2025, the US began gradually easing sanctions, and in November of that year, al-Sharaa was received by US President Trump at the White House. The two met again on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Ankara in July 2026. In early 2026, the US withdrew its military forces from Syria, and on Monday (August 24), it officially removed the country from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.
However, under the current circumstances, Syria appears to be relying primarily on itself, including in its relations with Turkey. For analyst Marcus Schneider, however, a potential Turkish presence is not comparable to the former Iranian presence during the Assad regime.
Contrary to the view held in Israel, he argues that Ankara is primarily interested in a stable Syria and in securing its southern border. "The idea that Turkey, a NATO member, would attack Israel, a nuclear power, is preposterous," he said. The real problem, he argues, is that Israel increasingly views Turkey as a strategic adversary and interprets Turkey's capabilities as evidence of hostile intentions.
Al-Sharaa is seeking foreign policy support wherever he can find it, observes Scheller. "In recent months, Turkey has increasingly become one of the countries from which Damascus expects concrete assistance." This is not just a matter of security: Ankara wants to expand its regional influence and, at the same time, has an interest in maintaining stability along the shared border, she said.
Who will ultimately determine Syria's security order?
Following the overthrow of Syria's longtime ruler Bashar Assad in December 2024, Israel established a security zone north of the Golan Heights and has repeatedly attacked Syrian targets. According to an analysis by the Carnegie Foundation, the calls for such a buffer zone is deeply rooted in Israeli security thinking; less clear, however, is the intention — sometimes attributed to Israel by analysts — of permanently fragmenting Syria to keep it weak.
The US think tank FDD takes a different view, pointing to Israel's skepticism toward the new Syrian military and Turkish support. However, Schneider notes that the new regime in Syria has extended a hand to Israel from the outset, despite its ideological origins. "Damascus does not want a war with Israel," he said, adding that it wants to regain its national sovereignty. It is precisely this aspiration that clashes with Israel's military presence and its red lines.
Syria needs a viable political order
"Syria is caught between two militarily powerful neighbors that respect neither its sovereignty nor its territorial integrity," said Scheller.
In her view, the outcome will now depend on al-Sharaa's negotiating skills. "How can he defend Syrian sovereignty against these two neighbors and actually chart a distinct Syrian path?" However, Syria's weakness does not lie solely in its military inferiority. The country must first develop a viable political order, she notes.
This is also the starting point for political scientist Haid Haid in an analysisfor the British think tank Chatham House: "Syria's foreign policy success has been significant, but it cannot, on its own, secure stability. In this sense, Syria's greatest vulnerability lies not at its borders, but within."
This article was originally published in German.

Iran says the U.S. is standing in the way of Hormuz deal amid talks with Oman
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:13:53 UTC
22:13:53 KST

The U.S. is obstructing an agreement between Iran and Oman to secure a safe transit route through the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Republic's hard-line Revolutionary Guard said Wednesday.
Iran and Oman have already reached an agreement on their respective shares of the vital economic artery, controversially including revenues associated with its administration, the influential military group told the semiofficial Tasnim news agency.
The Revolutionary Guard said the strait would remain closed if the U.S. does not accept Iran's conditions.
It came after Iran and Oman said in a joint statement Tuesday that their respective foreign ministers had discussed a "proposed framework" to establish "a joint temporary navigational corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines."
Oil prices have extended recent losses in response to the statement, with international benchmark Brent crude falling below the $90 per barrel mark overnight.
Just five commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, below the 10-day average of 15, according to preliminary data from Kpler. Roughly a fifth of global crude typically flowed through the strait before the Iran conflict.
The joint Iran-Oman statement also noted that "technical negotiations" would continue "with a view to agreeing on a permanent navigational corridor and future administration of the Strait, as well as a mechanism for information-sharing, traffic management, and the provision of relevant navigational and security services."
Contributing to pressure on oil prices in recent days, the U.S. has reportedly started returning its diplomats to Gulf states – suggesting Washington does not currently expect military escalation. Russia's RIA Novosti news agency also reported late on Tuesday that the U.S. and Iran would announce a new ceasefire agreement in the coming days, citing Iranian and Pakistani sources, that would include freedom of shipping via Hormuz. However, this could not be independently verified, and the White House did not respond to MS NOW's request for comment.
U.S. holds back on secondary sanctions
It comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's pledge on Monday to launch an "economic D-day" on the Iranian regime, threatening to target Tehran's "enablers" and trading partners in efforts to strangle its economy. This included a list of 60 individuals, entities and vessels.
However, the U.S. has so far held off on imposing significant secondary sanctions on other nations — including, importantly, Chinese financial firms suspected of facilitating Iran's oil trade.
"Why would I want to blow up the global financial system? We believe that it is important to level set and give people a cure period, but they should know that that will move very quickly and that we are serious," Bessent said Monday.
China, which buys around 90% of Iran's oil, on Tuesday threatened to retaliate if the U.S. opted to expand economic pressure on nations trading with Tehran.
Beijing "will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its rights and interests," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Tuesday.

There will no longer be a need to go down into &quot;Metrograd&quot; — six new surface crossings will be installed at Bessarabska Square in Kyiv.
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
16:13:51 EEST
22:13:51 KST

There will no longer be a need to go down into "Metrograd" — six new surface crossings will be installed at Bessarabska Square in Kyiv.
Kyiv • UNN
The underground crossings near Bessarabska Square will be duplicated with surface crossings. Traffic lights, tactile paving, and barrier-free routes are planned.
In Kyiv, the pedestrian traffic scheme around Bessarabska Square will be radically reorganized in the near future. The underground passages will be duplicated with above-ground crossings to create more convenient and accessible routes for pedestrians. This was stated by Konstantin Usov, Deputy Head of the Kyiv City State Administration for the Exercise of Self-Government Powers, as reported by UNN.
"All underground pedestrian passages around Bessarabska Square that run through the Metrograd shopping mall will be duplicated with safe above-ground pedestrian crossings. The work will begin shortly," Konstantin Usov said.
The new crossings will run across Taras Shevchenko Boulevard, Bessarabskyi Passage, Velyka Vasylkivska Street, and Baseina Street. A new traffic organization scheme was developed and approved for this purpose, and it was agreed upon by the Patrol Police Department in Kyiv.
Traffic and pedestrian signals will be installed at the pedestrian crossings. The curbs will also be lowered for the convenience of people with disabilities and other people with reduced mobility. To improve navigation for people with visual impairments, tactile paving will be installed, along with push buttons that activate audible signals during the pedestrian green light.
Specific changes are planned for Bessarabskyi Passage. An above-ground crossing will be arranged along Baseina Street. An additional sidewalk will be built on the Arena City side to create a safe pedestrian route from Lesi Ukrainky Street to Khreshchatyk Street and Taras Shevchenko Boulevard. Traffic lanes will also be redistributed, and a controlled entrance to the underground parking lot will be provided.
As part of the project, the pedestrian crossing between Bessarabsky Market and Krutyi Uzviz Street will also be upgraded in accordance with modern standards.
To organize parking and provide spaces for vehicles belonging to people with disabilities, a parking zone will be arranged between Bessarabsky Market and Arena City. The traffic organization scheme also provides for bicycle crossings adjacent to pedestrian crossings across Taras Shevchenko Boulevard, on Velyka Vasylkivska and Baseina streets, as well as Bessarabskyi Passage.
In total, six new above-ground crossings will be arranged in the Bessarabsky quarter to duplicate the underground passages, and two existing ones will be reconstructed. The pedestrian crossing between Khreshchatyk Street and Bessarabsky Market already provides an accessible route for Kyiv residents and visitors to the capital.
After the traffic organization scheme is implemented, pedestrians will be able to cross the streets using above-ground crossings, without having to use underground routes with stairs. This will create an integrated, barrier-free pedestrian route around Bessarabska Square that is convenient for people of different ages and with different needs.

Ratcliffe Visits Moscow
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:13:48 UTC
22:13:48 KST

Early Tuesday morning, Kyiv Post reported that on Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, “the US has again declined to join a United Nations statement condemning Russia’s attacks on Ukraine and calling for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire.”
The “why” – at least part of the why – presented itself later in the day when social media exploded with reports that a US Air Force C-17A reportedly had landed at Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
It’s hard to keep anything a secret anymore as “OSINT analysts tracked its route: on Aug. 23, the aircraft, callsign RCH4555 and registration 07-7181, flew from Charleston via Joint Base Andrews near Washington to Riga. This morning, it departed Riga without a publicly listed destination.”
CBS News reported the passenger on the C-17 was CIA Director John Ratcliffe.
CNN reported that “the US asked Ukraine to halt drone and missile strikes in Moscow and other cities in the north of Russia ahead of Ratcliffe’s trip” Monday through Wednesday, telling Ukraine that a senior US official would be traveling in Russia.
The why seems apparent – get Russian President Vladimir Putin back to the negotiation table, which probably explains why the US declined to join the UN statement condemning Russia’s attacks on Ukraine. The White House didn’t want to “poison the well” before the meeting took place.
Ukraine Strikes Russian Military Network, Hitting Radar, Drone Center, Key Supply Depots
Ukraine obliged – President Volodymyr Zelensky had tried on multiple occasions to get Russia to agree to a ceasefire.
But why Ratcliffe?
Unlike US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, Ratcliff brings a different skill set to the table – one that a former KGB agent would likely respect.
It’s safe to say that the Witkoff & Kushner buddy-buddy approach and business deals are off the table and that a more direct approach to bring the war to a conclusion is. Giving Putin the US intelligence assessment of his current situation – versus what his generals are telling him – may shock him to the negotiation table.
And why now?
Witkoff & Kusher have been a little busy with Iranian negotiations – better described by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as “passing messages between Pakistan and Qatar mediators.” That, and Kusher was recently dispatched to meet with minority leader Representative Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) ahead of the November elections to discuss potential areas of common ground should the Democrats retake the House.
But the most likely reason – the path to escalation is on a fast track.
Not a nuclear war – but a World War that could potentially drag NATO, North Korea, Belarus and China into Putin’s quest to conquer Ukraine.
Here’s why
- Russian casualties now total 1,479,300 – up another 1,230 today; 42,860 casualties in the month of July, with no end in sight. The Kremlin keeps sending them into the “meat grinder” and Ukrainian drones make them go away. Rinse and repeat daily.
- According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Putin is preparing to launch a new wave of mobilization following the Russian State Duma elections on Sept. 21 – drafting as many as 300,000 to 500,000 more troops.
- North Korea is prepared to deploy another 30,000-50,000 soldiers, ballistic missile launchers, KN-23/KN-24 missiles and their crews to Russia. Putin remains fixated on the Donbas.
- The Kremlin is 0-15 on Putin deadlines to capture the region since the invasion in February 2022. But they continue to press – like Big 10 Football in the 80s, “three yards and a cloud of dust.” Kyiv Post cites an Institute for the Study of War estimate that “at the current rate of advance [which on some parts of the front… has slowed to as little as 15-70 meters (49-230 feet) per day, described as record-low rates in more than a century of modern warfare] Russian forces are unlikely to capture the remaining parts of Donbas by the end of 2026 and may never achieve the objective.”
- A Russian lawmaker has said Moscow should complete its war against Ukraine by 2030 to prepare for what he described as a potential future confrontation with NATO.
- The Atlantic Council reports that Russia is “likely to expand attacks on the country’s civilian population and critical infrastructure in the coming months… [in order to] break Ukraine’s resistance.” As we wrote in The Hill back in January 2024, Putin has returned to a strategy of weaponizing winter.
Ukraine has no intention of backing down.
- The Ukrainian Armed Forces has recaptured 288 square miles of Russian-occupied land this year across its southeastern front.
- While the White House has backed away from granting Ukraine license to produce Patriot interceptor missiles – to defend themselves against Russian ballistic missile attacks – the United Kingdom and France have stepped-up and agreed to give Ukraine approval to produce long-range Storm Shadow / SCALP missiles – missiles that can be used to target Russian missile launch sites, storage facilities, production and assembly plants, and command and control centers.
- Ukraine is looking to add an active defense to the three-fold strategy we described in last week’s INTREP360 to defeat Russia. The introduction of the Fire Point 7 and 9 ballistic missiles will provide additional arrows in Zelensky’s quiver.
- As reported in the Financial Times, “Ukraine is seeking approval to use Starlink-equipped drones against ballistic missile launchers up to 200km inside Russia as Kyiv faces a severe shortage of air-defense interceptors. The move would require approval from Elon Musk, whose stance towards Ukraine and its use of his satellite internet service has oscillated.”
- Ukraine also expects to receive a timeline for further work on Freyja, a joint anti-ballistic missile system project by European and Ukrainian defense companies. Norway confirmed a $9 billion financial support package outside the EU framework to help finance the Freyja project.
- Ukraine also received confirmation that it will receive several Crotale air defense systems and their VT-1 missiles, as well as AIM missiles and additional missiles for Patriot systems.
Russia responded to the technology transfer by threatening the UK – never mind the Kremlin’s use of Iranian drones and North Korean ballistic missiles – and dragging Japan into the mix with the Kuril Islands.
Conditions are being set for a prolonged war that could expand rapidly.
Ratcliffe’s mission was to “cool the engines.” A new tactic has emerged – America is delivering a message to the aggressor – Russia. De-escalate in Ukraine, or risk World War III.

Court rejects request by convicted traitor for early release
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:12:00 UTC
22:12:00 KST

Court rejects request by convicted traitor for early release
Harju District Court ruled on Tuesday that it will not grant convicted traitor Deniss Metsavas's request for early release under electronic monitoring.
The Prosecutor's Office does not support Metsavas's conditional early release, and the prosecutor maintained that position during the hearing. Tallinn Prison likewise does not support allowing the inmate to continue serving his sentence under electronic monitoring supervised by a probation officer.
Metsavas's defense argued that through his conduct and efforts, he has shown that he has drawn the necessary conclusions from his crimes and that continued imprisonment is not strictly necessary to guide his behavior.
When deciding on conditional early release, the court considers the circumstances of the crime, the offender's personality and prior life, behavior during imprisonment — including participation in activities that reduce the risk of reoffending or willingness to participate in such activities during supervision — as well as living conditions and the potential consequences of early release.
The court reviewed the submitted materials, written opinions from the prosecutor and defense, and heard the prosecutor, the convict and his attorney. Based on this, the court concluded that early release would be premature and unjustified.
The court agreed with the defense that Metsavas has several positive factors supporting early release: a stable place to live, supportive family members, vocational training completed during imprisonment, work in various positions such as librarian and instructor of math and yoga groups, no unpaid claims, and savings in his release fund.
However, the court noted that these positive factors alone do not guarantee lawful behavior after release. Metsavas also had a job, home, family and supportive relatives before imprisonment, yet still committed serious crimes.
The main substantive condition for early release is a reliable forecast that the inmate will behave lawfully in the future. Despite the positive aspects, the court considers the risk of reoffending to be high.
This assessment is supported by the seriousness of Metsavas's first‑degree crime, committed over a long period. In the court's view, the risk of new offenses has not been sufficiently reduced.
The ruling has not yet entered into force.
The court convicted Metsavas of treason in 2018 and sentenced him to 15 years in prison.
--
Editor: Karin Koppel, Argo Ideon

US economy grows by 1.5% in Q2
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:11:57 UTC
22:11:57 KST

Gokhan Ergocun
26 August 2026•Update: 26 August 2026
The US economy grew by 1.5% in the second quarter of this year, in line with market forecasts, the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) announced on Wednesday.
According to the official report, growth in the US economy during the second quarter was driven by increases in consumer spending, exports, and investment, which were partially offset by a decline in government spending.
Imports also rose during the same period.
The increase recorded in the personal consumption expenditure price index for the second quarter of this year was at 5.3%. 
The increase in the core personal consumption expenditures price index— excludes food and energy expenditures—was at 3.6% for the same period. 
The US economy had recorded 2.1% growth in the first quarter of this year.

Russian troops liberate two communities in Ukraine operation over past day — top brass
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:11:55 UTC
22:11:55 KST

MOSCOW, August 26. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated two communities in the Sumy and Zaporozhye Regions over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units took control of the settlement of Pisarevka in the Sumy Region through decisive operations. <…> Battlegroup East units kept advancing deep into the enemy’s defenses and liberated the settlement of Nezhenka in the Zaporozhye Region through active operations," the ministry said in a statement.
Kiev loses 1,405 troops along engagement line in past day – latest figures
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,405 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost roughly 240 troops, a tank and 14 motor vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, about 210 troops and two US-made armored vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and more than 215 troops and four field artillery guns in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 365 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, over 345 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and about 30 troops and a howitzer in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicts 240 casualties on Ukrainian army in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted roughly 240 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy tank and 14 motor vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, two airmobile brigades of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Tolstodubovo, Proletarskoye, Sadki and Kiyanitsa in the Sumy Region," the ministry said.
In the Kharkov direction, Battlegroup North units inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade, an assault regiment, an unmanned systems battalion of the Ukrainian army, three territorial defense brigades and a National Guard brigade in areas near the settlements of Prikolotnoye, Buzovo, Tsupovka, Novoaleksandrovka, Liptsy and Slatino in the Kharkov Region, the ministry reported.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 240 personnel, a tank and 14 motor vehicles in those frontline areas over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicts 210 casualties on Ukrainian army in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted roughly 210 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two US-made armored vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Proletarskoye and Vyssheye Solyonoye in the Kharkov Region, Bogorodichnoye, Sidorovo, Mayaki, Raigorodok and Svyatogorsk in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 210 personnel, two US-made HMMWV armored vehicles, 17 pickup trucks and an electronic warfare station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicts over 215 casualties on Ukrainian army in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 215 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed four enemy field artillery guns in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on formations of three mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade, an assault brigade, an airmobile brigade, a mountain assault brigade and an unmanned systems battalion of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Kramatorsk, Slavyansk, Druzhkovka, Krasny Molochar, Nikolayevka, Semyonovka and Alekseyevo-Druzhkovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 215 personnel, 25 motor vehicles and four field artillery guns in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicts over 365 casualties on Ukrainian army in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted more than 365 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units continued advancing deep into the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a jaeger brigade of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and four National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Raiskoye, Andreyevka, Druzhkovka, Slavyanka, Novogrigorovka, Novotroitskoye, Belozerskoye, Dobropolye and Roganskoye in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 365 personnel, a Kozak armored combat vehicle, five motor vehicles, an artillery gun and an electronic warfare station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicts over 345 casualties on Ukrainian army in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 345 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup East units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two assault brigades, two air assault brigades, three assault regiments, an unmanned systems battalion of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Malinovka, Malomikhailovka, Ivanovka and Vasilkovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Obshcheye, Barvinovka and Omelnik in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 345 personnel, two armored combat vehicles and three motor vehicles in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminates 30 Ukrainian troops in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 30 Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy howitzer in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade and a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Orekhov, Dimitrovo, Novoyakovlevka, Chervonaya Krinitsa and Preobrazhenka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 30 [Ukrainian] military personnel, 32 motor vehicles, a 122mm D-30 howitzer and three electronic warfare stations were destroyed," it said.
Russian troops strike logistics centers, energy sites used by Ukrainian army in past day
Russian troops struck logistics centers, energy infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army and enemy deployment sites over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck logistics centers, fuel and energy, transport and port infrastructure facilities in Ukraine used by the Ukrainian army, ammunition and materiel depots, workshops assembling and sites storing unmanned aerial vehicles and their components, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 141 locations," the ministry said.
Russian air defenses intercept 798 Ukrainian UAVs, 12 smart bombs over past day
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 798 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and 12 smart bombs over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down 12 guided aerial bombs, a rocket of the US-made HIMARS multiple launch rocket system, three Flamingo long-range cruise missiles and 798 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Russian forces destroy over 220,000 military drones in Ukraine operation
Russian forces have destroyed more than 220,000 unmanned aerial vehicles of the Ukrainian army since the start of the special military operation in Ukraine, the ministry reported.
"Overall, the following targets have been destroyed since the start of the special military operation: 674 aircraft, 284 helicopters, 220,067 unmanned aerial vehicles, 669 surface-to-air missile systems, 30,725 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,775 multiple rocket launchers, 36,274 field artillery guns and mortars and 70,240 special military motor vehicles," the ministry said.

Feature: Wuxi Symphony Orchestra shares Chinese cultural charm with Italian audiences through music
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:35 CST
22:11:35 KST

ROME, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Under the stars on Tuesday night, the powerful and expressive sound of suona soloist Zhang Qianyuan filled an open-air amphitheater in the Italian town of Tuscania. The vibrant notes of the traditional Chinese wind instrument evoked the ancient Silk Road heritage of Dunhuang, in northwest China's Gansu Province, while the violin, cello, trumpet and harp added layers of Western orchestral colors.
The scene came from the second movement of Flying Apsaras, an original symphonic suite by the Wuxi Symphony Orchestra. As part of the Tuscania Summer Festival 2026, around 70 musicians from the orchestra performed for more than 200 Italian audience members under the stars, presenting a concert that blended Chinese musical elements with Western symphonic traditions.
In addition to Flying Apsaras, the orchestra performed renowned Western works, including Giuseppe Verdi's "The Sicilian Vespers" and Johannes Brahms' "Symphony No. 1." The event was organized by the non-profit social promotion association The Arts Crossroad.
"Flying Apsaras was composed by our orchestra's music director Li Shaosheng. It tells the story of humanity's journey from curiosity about the unknown universe to space exploration, as well as China's rapid development in aerospace technology. It celebrates the Chinese spirit of space exploration," said Wu Ximing, chairman of Wuxi Symphony Orchestra Co., Ltd.
Wu explained that the inclusion of traditional Chinese elements was intended to help international audiences better understand the cultural message behind the work. The suona part in the second movement and the vocal performance by Chinese tenor Xue Haoyin in the fifth movement were both designed to highlight the Chinese identity of the composition.
By combining traditional Chinese sounds with Western orchestral expression, Flying Apsaras offered Italian audiences a different perspective on contemporary Chinese music.
For Chieko Hata, president of The Arts Crossroad Association, the young age and dedication of the Wuxi Symphony Orchestra's musicians were among the main reasons why the orchestra was invited.
"One of the most attractive things about this orchestra is that the average age of its members is only 28," Hata said. "I really think that Chinese musicians have a very strong work ethic. They practice hard and always want to become better."
She added that the orchestra's spirit matched the mission of the festival, which focuses on supporting young musicians.
"We thought this orchestra could also inspire Italian and European young people, showing them that music belongs to everyone and that young musicians can perform at an exceptionally high level while still enjoying what they do," Hata said.
The concert received an enthusiastic response from local audiences. The amphitheater's original stone seating was soon filled, forcing organizers to add temporary chairs. Even then, some spectators stood outside the railings to watch the performance. One mother even brought her baby daughter to experience her very first concert.
"I saw the orchestra perform here yesterday for the first time, and it gave me a feeling of peace and tranquility," said local audience member Marta Scriboni. "After last night's concert, I immediately bought a ticket for tonight, and I came back again with great enthusiasm."
Tuscania Mayor Fabio Bartolacci said the concert represented more than just a musical event.
"This event has an important impact from cultural, tourism, and, of course, economic perspectives," Bartolacci said. "As a very welcoming town, we hope this marks the beginning of a long-term cultural journey and a lasting relationship between the music coming from China and the artistic heritage represented by our town."
The Wuxi Symphony Orchestra's European tour included five performances in Slovenia, Austria and Italy. The Tuscania concert marked the final stop of the tour. ■

China's top political advisor calls for efforts to enhance people's welfare
China

2026-08-26
21:11:34 CST
22:11:34 KST

Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) National Committee, presides over and addresses the closing meeting of the 18th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th CPPCC National Committee in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 26, 2026. The Standing Committee of the 14th CPPCC National Committee closed its 18th session on Wednesday under the theme of ensuring and improving people's livelihoods. (Xinhua/Rao Aimin)
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- China's top political advisor Wang Huning on Wednesday urged members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) to adhere to the principle of serving the people and assist the Party and the government in improving people's welfare.
Wang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the CPPCC National Committee, made the remarks while addressing the closing meeting of a standing committee session of the CPPCC National Committee.
Noting that realizing common prosperity is an important goal of socialist modernization, Wang called on CPPCC members to make more insightful suggestions and do more practical work for the people during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030).
Political advisors should work to implement the decisions and arrangements made by the CPC and the Chinese government, and ensure that the achievements of China's modernization benefit all people more fairly, Wang said.
Wang also attended a plenary meeting of the standing committee session of the CPPCC National Committee on Wednesday. Fourteen standing committee members of the CPPCC National Committee spoke on the theme of ensuring and improving people's livelihoods. ■

Death toll hits 22 in flash flood in Nepal: police
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:32 CST
22:11:32 KST

KATHMANDU, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- The death toll from a massive flash flood in Nepal's Bhote Koshi River on Wednesday reached 22, the police said.
Rajendra Prasad Dhamala, spokesperson for the Bagmati Province Police, confirmed the death toll and said search and rescue operations were continuing in the affected areas.
Security forces have so far rescued 88 people from the affected areas, Dhamala said.
The Nepal Tourism Board said that as many as 384 tourists, including 291 foreigners, have been reported missing after a massive flash flood swept through Rasuwa district in northern Nepal.
Sunil Sharma, spokesperson at the board, said the missing foreign tourists were from India, Australia, the Netherlands, the United States, Malaysia, Britain and South Africa, among others.
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called an emergency cabinet meeting to discuss rescue and relief measures.
The Nepali Army, backed by other security forces, has intensified search and rescue operations in the affected districts.
The worst damage has been reported in Rasuwa, where the flood swept away several houses, damaging markets, hydropower projects, roads and other infrastructure.
"Several people are reported missing. Rescue efforts are underway," Druba Prasad Adhikari, deputy chief district officer of Rasuwa, told Xinhua earlier. ■

3 killed, 19 injured in Ukrainian strikes across Russian regions
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:28 CST
22:11:28 KST

MOSCOW, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Three people were killed and 19 others injured in Ukrainian attacks on several Russian regions, local authorities said on Wednesday.
A man and a 14-year-old were killed and two women injured after a drone strike triggered a house fire in the Lipetsk region, Governor Igor Artamonov said.
In the Belgorod region, a woman was killed in a drone attack in the Grayvoronsky district, acting Governor Alexander Shuvaev said, adding that another 12 people were injured in seven other districts.
Two people were wounded by window fragments from a downed drone in the Voronezh region, while another man was injured by falling drone debris in the Tula region, according to local officials.
In Tambov region, regional Governor Yevgeny Pervyshov said 16 drones had been destroyed, yet another three drones managed to strike a local warehouse. The strike sparked a fire and left two people injured.
The Russian Defense Ministry said early Wednesday that its air defenses had intercepted 426 Ukrainian drones overnight over several Russian regions. ■

Namibian president calls for unity in struggle for economic emancipation
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:27 CST
22:11:27 KST

WINDHOEK, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah said on Wednesday that economic emancipation has become the country's new national struggle, urging citizens to unite against poverty, unemployment, inequality and corruption.
Addressing a Heroes' Day ceremony at Heroes' Acre in Windhoek marking the 60th anniversary of the start of Namibia's armed liberation struggle, Nandi-Ndaitwah said the country has achieved political freedom and sovereignty but must now improve the material conditions of its people.
"Thirty-six years after independence, ours is the struggle for economic emancipation," she said, calling for Namibia's natural resources to be used to improve the well-being of its citizens.
She identified poverty, youth unemployment, inequality, corruption, institutional inefficiency, hunger and homelessness as key challenges facing the current generation.
Nandi-Ndaitwah said her administration's development agenda, outlined in the Sixth National Development Plan, prioritizes natural resource beneficiation, value addition and youth empowerment.
"We cannot sustain ourselves on past glory alone. We honor the past most meaningfully when we build on what those before us sacrificed to achieve," she said.
The president also paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives during Namibia's liberation struggle and urged Namibians to build a country where peace is protected, integrity is upheld and prosperity becomes a reality for all citizens.
Heroes' Day, observed annually on Aug. 26, commemorates the 1966 Battle of Omugulugwombashe, which marked the beginning of Namibia's armed liberation struggle against South African apartheid rule. ■

Xi to attend SCO summit, pay state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:22 CST
22:11:22 KST

BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- From Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan and President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi of Egypt, the Chinese foreign ministry announced on Wednesday.
This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO. At the Bishkek Summit, Xi will have in-depth exchanges of views with participating leaders on deepening SCO cooperation in various fields under the new circumstances and major international and regional issues, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told a regular news briefing when asked for more information about the trip.
They will provide guidance for the SCO's high-quality development and participation in the reform and development of the global governance system, Lin said.
During his stay in Kyrgyzstan, Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations, cooperation in key areas, and international and regional situation with his Kyrgyz counterpart in their talks, and attend various state events, Lin noted.
Lin said China looks forward to working with Kyrgyzstan to take this visit as an opportunity to promote high-quality development of mutually beneficial cooperation on all fronts, add new dimensions to the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, and bring more benefits to the two peoples.
The Egypt leg of Xi's trip, his first state visit to the country in a decade, coincides with the 70th anniversary of bilateral diplomatic ties, the spokesperson said.
The Chinese and Egyptian presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest, according to Lin.
Through the visit, China looks forward to working with Egypt to carry forward traditional friendship, render each other firm support, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and bolster each other's modernization, thereby jointly drawing a new chapter of bilateral relations and contributing to regional and world peace and stability, Lin added. ■

Helicopter crash leaves 2 dead near Turin, Italy
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:22 CST
22:11:22 KST

ROME, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Two people were killed Wednesday morning when an aircraft crashed near a dam in northern Italy's Piedmont region, local media said.
The crash occurred at around 11:30 a.m. local time near the Campiccioli dam in the Antrona Schieranco area near the region's capital city of Turin, according to Ansa news.
The victims were a 60-year-old man and a 63-year-old woman, Ansa said.
Air rescue services were dispatched to the crash site.
Initial reports indicated that the aircraft was an autogyro, also known as a gyroplane, rather than a conventional helicopter. An autogyro is equipped with an overhead rotor that is not directly connected to the engine.
Authorities are investigating the cause of the crash. ■

It is the first time that the all the exhibition halls have been booked by exhibitors at Gamescom 2026. The number of exhibitors has hit a record high and the scale of the exhibition zone for independent game developers, which is devoted to showcasing the creativity and products of small teams is also unprecedented, Felix Falk, managing director of the German Games Industry Association said and added that they are a sign of the attraction of the gaming culture.

Feature: Chinese-built roads transform western Kenya's breadbasket
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:11:06 CST
22:11:06 KST

ELDORET, Kenya, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- For decades, life in Uasin Gishu County, western Kenya's agricultural heartland, was defined by maize and milk.
While its rolling fields fed the nation, local farmers routinely faced delays waiting for grain board payments, hampered by a degraded road network.
That familiar landscape is rapidly evolving. A combination of new highways, agri-tech innovation, and expanded global market access is rewriting the economic narrative of one of Kenya's primary breadbaskets.
Central to this transformation is a sweeping infrastructure drive led by Chinese engineering firms under the Belt and Road Initiative, whose newly carved transit arteries are reshaping the movement of agricultural goods across the region.
Anchoring this regional growth is the approximately 32-km Eldoret Bypass, constructed by China Wu Yi Company Limited.
By diverting heavy freight away from Eldoret's congested city center, the bypass has created a seamless transit route for cargo bound for Uganda, Rwanda, and South Sudan.
Crucial feeder corridors such as the Cheplasgei-Maili Tisa road have also reduced farm-to-terminal travel times by half.
Thanks to these upgraded road networks, local farmers are diversifying beyond traditional maize cultivation into high-value exports like avocados, French beans, cut flowers, and passion fruit. Integrated digital agri-tech platforms now allow smallholders to aggregate produce, monitor cold-chain logistics, and access international markets.
With improved transit times, crops harvested at dawn can be processed at Eldoret International Airport by evening, reaching European and Middle Eastern supermarket shelves within 36 hours.
Local dairy farmer John Korir recalled his past struggles before the infrastructure upgrades, noting that getting fresh milk to processing plants was a constant race against time.
On unpaved, mud-slicked roads during the rainy season, transport delays frequently caused milk to spoil before reaching buyers, resulting in heavy financial losses for his household.
Today, Korir said the paved road network has completely transformed his operation.
Collection trucks now reach his farm gate reliably twice a day, allowing him to deliver fresh yields without fear of spoilage, secure stable income, and re-invest in expanding his herd.
"Five years ago, I would stay with my milk for over four hours in Eldoret town traffic before reaching the New Kenya Cooperative Creameries plant, but today it takes me 45 minutes to deliver my milk to the plant," Korir told Xinhua during a recent interview.
For dairy farmers in Kenya's North Rift, tarmac has become the decisive boundary between profit and loss.
While Uasin Gishu County produces over 300 million liters of milk annually, its primary bottleneck has historically been logistics rather than production.
Unreliable dirt roads frequently stranded raw yields in transit, turning highly perishable milk sour before it could reach processing plants.
"Milk spoils in traffic and when we are stuck for over three hours, the cooler would struggle and our proceeds are deducted," said Korir.
Officials described the regional infrastructure buildout as a deliberate long-term strategy, noting that the new bypasses and inter-county corridors were specifically planned to unlock the area's economic potential.
"The road networks we championed, from the bypasses to regional inter-county links, were built with a clear strategy to transform Eldoret into a natural assembly and transit point for Eastern Africa. The dividends of those infrastructure decisions are now paying off," said former Uasin Gishu Governor and current Senator Jackson Mandago.
Willy Kenei, chairman of the Kenya National Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Uasin Gishu, highlighted the transformation, pointing to surging industrial land values along the newly constructed bypass corridors.
Asphalt is rolling across the Rift Valley, digital platforms are linking smallholders to freighters, and Eldoret's new city status is cementing its role as a continental hub.
The story of Uasin Gishu is no longer confined to maize silos and milk tankers. It is a story of a granary building itself a runway to the world. ■

HARARE, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) on Wednesday hailed the sustained decline in the local Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) annual inflation, which hit 2.9 percent in August, its lowest level since independence in 1980.
In a statement, the country's central bank noted that Zimbabwe has maintained a single-digit ZiG annual inflation rate for eight consecutive months since January, marking a significant milestone toward price stability and macroeconomic confidence.
The bank added that annual ZiG inflation has averaged 4.2 percent over the first seven months of 2026 and is expected to remain stable within single-digit levels in the medium to long term.
Sustaining single-digit inflation for 24 months is one of eight conditions required before Zimbabwe transitions from a multi-currency system to exclusive use of the ZiG, according to the RBZ.
Data released Tuesday by the Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (ZIMSTAT) showed monthly ZiG inflation held steady at 0.1 percent in August.
In U.S. dollar terms, August monthly inflation dropped to 0.0 percent from 0.3 percent in July, while the annual rate remained unchanged at 3.1 percent. ZIMSTAT credited ongoing exchange rate stability for keeping both ZiG and U.S. dollar inflation low. ■

BANGKOK, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's Constitutional Court is set to rule on Sept. 28 whether barcodes and QR codes printed on ballots violated the charter's guarantee of voting secrecy, in a case that could lead to the February general election being annulled.
In a statement on Wednesday, the court set the ruling date after hearing testimonies from five witnesses, noting that the fact-finding phase has now closed and ordered associated parties to submit written closing statements by Sept. 11.
The court found it necessary to conduct an on-site evidence inspection on Thursday, assigning two judges and court officials to inspect the ballot storage sites, ballot stubs, unused ballots, voter rolls, and election materials used in the Feb. 8 election in Bangkok.
In March, the court accepted a petition filed by the country's Ombudsman arguing that the barcodes and QR codes printed on ballot papers could potentially be used to trace and identify individual voters and their selections.
The Ombudsman said it had received 22 complaints urging it to refer the matter to the Constitutional Court against the Election Commission and associated parties, arguing that the design of the ballots made it possible to trace a voter's identity and cross-check it against how they voted, implying that ballots were not cast in secret. ■

Macao airport pilots cargo operations in south China's Guangdong

Unknown Publisher

ZHUHAI, Guangdong, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Macao International Airport (MIA) on Wednesday launched pilot cargo palletization on neighboring Hengqin island in Zhuhai, south China's Guangdong Province, as part of its upstream cargo terminal project currently under construction.
This means that security screening and palletization, which is the stacking of goods for transportation, for cargo shipped from the Chinese mainland to overseas destinations via Macao will be gradually expanded from MIA to Hengqin.
Construction of the Hengqin cargo terminal, located about 13 kilometers from MIA, began in October 2025, with a planned gross floor area of approximately 97,600 square meters. It is scheduled to be completed by the end of 2026 and become officially operational in the first half of 2027, serving as an extension of MIA for security screening and palletization to facilitate cargo transport between the mainland and Macao.
The pilot palletization took place at a logistics center near the Hengqin terminal project site. Later on Wednesday, the cargo, comprising e-commerce goods and daily-use items such as toys and watches, was transported via Hengqin Port to MIA, bound for Malaysia and the Philippines.
Sam Hou Fai, chief executive of the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR), Guangdong Vice Governor Zhang Guozhi, and several other officials from Macao and Guangdong attended a launch ceremony for the pilot palletization initiative.
Ng Wai Han, secretary for economy and finance of the Macao SAR government, said at the ceremony that the launch of the pilot palletization marked an important milestone in the project, adding that Macao and Hengqin will seize this opportunity to further improve their trade and logistics ecosystems.
The construction of the Hengqin cargo terminal has been listed as one of the tasks aimed at supporting Hong Kong and Macao SARs in better integrating into and serving the country's overall development under China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). It is also included in Macao's third five-year plan for economic and social development for the same period, released by the SAR government last week.
According to the SAR's plan, the terminal is expected to be capable of handling 300,000 tonnes of cargo per year, three times MIA's current annual air cargo processing capacity of roughly 100,000 tonnes. ■

SUVA, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Fiji is stepping up efforts to expand hydroponics and protected agriculture as part of a broader push to increase year-round vegetable production, reduce reliance on food imports and strengthen national food security.
Minister for Agriculture and Waterways Tomasi Tunabuna said controlled-environment farming could help farmers maintain a more stable supply of vegetables when seasonal conditions affect conventional production, reported local news on Wednesday.
Protected agriculture, including greenhouse and other controlled growing systems, can allow farmers to better manage temperature, moisture, pests and other growing conditions, while hydroponic systems enable crops to be cultivated without conventional soil-based production.
The approaches are particularly relevant to Fiji's efforts to maintain vegetable supplies during periods when adverse weather or seasonal conditions disrupt production.
Tunabuna said more consistent domestic production would benefit not only local consumers but also Fiji's tourism industry, which depends on a reliable supply of fresh produce.
Fiji continues to rely significantly on imported food and other agricultural products.
According to the minister, the country imported about 1.1 billion U.S. dollars' worth of agricultural goods last year, underscoring the scale of the challenge facing efforts to increase domestic supply. ■

NEW DELHI, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- The Indian Medical Association (IMA), a body of doctors of modern medicine in India, on Wednesday warned against self-medicating with antibiotics amid a surge in H1N1 cases.

The exhibition “New Landscapes” by London-based Bulgarian artist Ruslan Kotev will be on display at Paris Art Gallery in Sofia from August 27 to September 12. The exhibition will feature around 15 paintings executed in an abstract and figurative-abstract style, the Bulgarian News Agency (BTA) reports.
“New Landscapes” is Ruslan Kotev’s fourth solo exhibition in Bulgaria. According to Nadya Pavlova, founder of Paris Art Gallery, light occupies a central place in the artist’s work. Kotev creates multilayered paintings in which landscape often serves as a starting point for exploring memory, absence and the perception of time. Among his preferred subjects are landscapes from Sicily and the United Kingdom, including dramatic seascapes and abandoned houses where human presence survives only as a trace, she notes.
PHOTO Paris Art Gallery in Sofia
“One might say that he paints portraits of absence. It is a state in which human presence is missing, while the houses have somehow begun to lead lives of their own, steeped in an irrepressible nostalgia for the past. Something is glimpsed in the distance, perhaps a church dome, rooftops or the silhouettes of trees, but nothing is ever sufficiently concrete,” Nadya Pavlova adds.

Fed’s preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
13:08:28 UTC
22:08:28 KST

Prices consumers pay for a variety of goods and services rose slightly in July, according to the Federal Reserve's main inflation gauge.
The personal consumption expenditures price index, which the Fed uses as its preferred forecasting tool, increased a seasonally adjusted 0.2% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.7%, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday. Both were 0.1 percentage point above the Dow Jones consensus.
But stripping out volatile food and energy costs, core PCE posted respective gains of 0.2% and 3.3%, in line with forecasts. While the Fed considers both measures, policymakers generally see core inflation as the better measure of longer-term trends.
The report also showed that personal income rose 0.4% while spending increased 0.2%, both stronger than expected.
Goods prices actually declined on the month, off 0.1%, driven by a 2.7% decrease in gasoline and other energy-related goods and a 0.9% drop in furnishings and long-lasting household equipment.
Services prices rose 0.3%, pushed by a 1.2% increase in financial services and insurance as well as a 0.3% gain in housing.
Stock market futures pulled back a bit after the report while Treasury yields were higher.
The report comes with Fed officials weighing their next policy move as inflation, despite generally soft monthly readings this summer, is still well above the central bank's 2% goal.
With the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee not meeting formally in August, officials have a bit of a respite before making a decision at their next gathering on Sept. 15-16. Markets are pricing in only about a 1 in 3 probability of a move then, with the best chance for a rate hike coming in December.
Though the FOMC doesn't meet, Fed officials this week gather at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, for their annual symposium, the highlight being a policy speech scheduled for Friday from Chairman Kevin Warsh.
Since taking office in May, Warsh has been circumspect about where he sees policy heading, instead preferring that markets set the tone.
Government bond yields have been on the rise lately. Both the 10- and 30-year Treasurys recently saw yields hit their highest levels since 2007, just before the global financial crisis. The surge has come from a variety of factors, including investors' concern about the Fed's commitment to its inflation target as well as debt and deficit issues with the federal budget.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent a week ago announced an initiative in which his department would step up its buybacks of government debt. However, market participants have expressed doubt about whether the move will have a meaningful impact on yields.

The Nishad community finds itself at the centre of the fish row in Ayodhya ahead of 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.
At a time when many Hindu devotees traditionally give up non-vegetarian food during 'Sawan', fish has acquired an unlikely political importance in Uttar Pradesh.The row began earlier this month with Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad's remark that fish cooked without garlic and onion could be considered vegetarian. It escalated on August 23, when a video purportedly showing fish being prepared at a Nishad community event in Ayodhya, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, surfaced on social media.But behind the sparring over what was - or was not - on Rai's plate lies a larger electoral calculation. The Nishad vote has shifted political loyalties before, and with the BJP seeking to retain its non-Yadav OBC coalition and the opposition trying to prise open that support, the community could once again become an important factor in the 2027 contest.
The 'fish on your plate' row
The controversy began earlier this month when Sanjay Nishad said at a programme: "Bina lahsun-pyaz ki bani machhli shakahari hai."The remark came during Sawan, a month when many Hindu devotees observe dietary restrictions, and quickly attracted attention because of the community he represents. Nishads have historically depended on rivers and water bodies for fishing, fish-rearing, boating and related livelihoods, making food and fishing practices part of a broader social and economic identity.
Then came Ayodhya.On August 23, UP Congress president Ajay Rai travelled to Tarun, around 30 km from Ayodhya, after visiting Hanumangarhi, reciting the Hanuman Chalisa and offering prayers at the Ram temple. He attended a programme organised by members of the Nishad community. A video showing fish being prepared at the venue subsequently surfaced.
Sanjay Nishad said fish preparation mattered.
The timing and location gave the BJP an opening.BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary described the alleged fish feast as "highly condemnable and unforgivable", while Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Rai of "duplicity" for visiting a temple and then attending a fish feast during Sawan."You saw the conduct of the Congress state president yesterday. He goes to Hanumangarhi for darshan and, after coming out, enjoys a fish feast and then shouts 'Ram-Ram'," Adityanath said.Rai denied eating fish and challenged the CM to produce evidence. "If he can produce any pictures, I will be ready to resign immediately," he said.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera defended the hosts, saying they belonged to the Nishad community and had their own traditions of eating and drinking.Later, cabinet minister Om Prakash Rajbhar entered the controversy, backing Nishad's earlier claim and asking Congress to clarify whether the fish allegedly served at the event had been cooked with garlic and onion."Sanjay Nishad machhli ke mahir hain, unhe zyada jaankari hai, hum thode kam hain," Rajbhar said.The political argument, however, goes well beyond the menu at one event. The larger story is the political importance of the community that hosted it.
Ajay Rai dared CM Yogi Adityanath to provide evidence.
Nishads — the 'jal kisans'
The Nishads are a cluster of riverine communities whose traditional livelihoods have been closely tied to rivers, ponds and other water bodies. Community organisations have increasingly used the term 'jal kisan', or water farmers, to describe this relationship.Fishing, fish-rearing, boating and the sale of fish have historically been central to these communities' economic lives. Questions over access to water bodies, fishing rights, sand mining and regulation of traditional occupations therefore have a direct political resonance.The term Nishad is also used as an umbrella for several communities and sub-castes, including Mallah, Kewat, Bind, Kashyap, Dhimar, Batham, Kahar, Manjhi and Turaha. Not all of these communities necessarily identify themselves as Nishad in the same way.
Organiser of the event defended the decision to keep fish in the menu.
In Uttar Pradesh, Nishads are classified among the Other Backward Classes (OBCs).Political estimates put the core Nishad population at around 4.5-5 per cent of the state's electorate. Estimates that include a wider set of related riverine communities put their combined share considerably higher.There is no recent official caste census providing a definitive figure, but the community's electoral importance comes less from its statewide percentage than from its concentration.Nishad voters have a significant presence across the Ganga-Yamuna belt and eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia, Mau, Ghazipur, Mirzapur, Bhadohi, Jaunpur and Prayagraj, besides parts of Sultanpur and Fatehpur.The community is considered electorally influential in more than 160 Assembly constituencies, with around 80 seats often identified as having a particularly substantial Nishad presence.That geographical concentration explains why a community accounting for a relatively small share of the state's electorate can command such political attention.
Estimated data based on reports.
Nishadraj and Ekalavya: The epic roots of identity
The Nishad political identity is also deeply connected to stories from the Hindu epics.In the Ramayana, Nishadraj Guha, the boatman-king, is described as an ally of Ram during his exile. Guha receives Ram, Sita and Lakshman and helps them cross the Ganga.
The 51-foot-high statue of Lord Ram and Nishadraj at Shringverpur Dham, 40 km from Prayagraj.
For the Nishad community, the story has long been invoked as a marker of their place within the Ram narrative — not as an identity created by contemporary politics, but as an older cultural association that acquired renewed political meaning during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.The community also invokes Ekalavya from the Mahabharata, who is traditionally identified as belonging to the Nishad community. His story - of a skilled archer seeking to learn from Dronacharya and ultimately giving his thumb as guru dakshina - has come to represent a different strand of Nishad memory: talent, exclusion and the struggle for recognition.The two figures capture contrasting elements of the community's epic imagination: Nishadraj represents proximity to and loyalty towards Ram, while Ekalavya represents ability denied recognition.These narratives have subsequently been woven into the community's assertion of a distinct historical and social identity.
The Ram Janmabhoomi movement
Sections of the community found their cultural resonance in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.As the campaign for a Ram temple in Ayodhya gathered momentum in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Nishad organisations and leaders participated in the wider mobilisation. The story of Nishadraj Guha gave the movement an immediate cultural connection for sections of the community, while the broader call for 'Ram Rajya' resonated with those who saw the temple campaign as a civilisational and cultural cause.The political landscape changed sharply after BJP leader LK Advani's Ram Rath Yatra in 1990, which transformed the temple issue into a mass political movement. The demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992, further entrenched Ayodhya as a defining issue in BJP politics.
Source: Centre for Study of Developing Societies Lokniti.
As the BJP expanded its support among non-Yadav OBC communities, sections of the Nishad community also moved towards the party.But that support did not become a permanent political contract.
From support to sense of being left behind
Among sections of Nishad political opinion, a recurring grievance emerged: the community had supported the Ram movement but did not receive a commensurate political return.The complaint has, at various points, extended to BJP leaders associated with the Ram movement, including Advani and former UP CM Kalyan Singh, with Nishad voices arguing that their support for the Ram cause did not translate into adequate representation or resolution of longstanding demands regarding representation and farming on the riverside.In the coming years, the same community that participated in the Ram movement subsequently moved towards the Samajwadi Party, created its own political organisation and entered into an alliance with the BJP.That fluidity became particularly visible in the 1990s.
Phoolan Devi and politics of representation
Before the emergence of the Nishad Party, the strongest political association for sections of the community came through the social-justice politics of the Samajwadi Party.Phoolan Devi became the most recognisable symbol of that phase.A Mallah woman from Uttar Pradesh, Phoolan Devi contested the Mirzapur Lok Sabha seat on an SP ticket in 1996 and won. She retained the seat in 1999.
SP has given key post to Phoolan Devi's sister ahead of 2027 polls.
Her rise gave the community an unusually prominent political figure and turned caste identity into a language of representation.Her political legacy continues to be invoked in Uttar Pradesh.
Nishad Party enters equation
The next major shift came in 2016, when Sanjay Nishad founded the Nirbal Indian Shoshit Hamara Aam Dal, popularly known as the Nishad Party.The party sought to consolidate riverine communities and give political expression to demands involving reservation, representation, fishing rights and livelihoods.Its first major electoral breakthrough came in an unlikely place.In the March 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha bypoll, Praveen Nishad, Sanjay Nishad's son, contested as an SP-backed candidate and defeated the BJP.The result was politically significant because Gorakhpur had been Yogi Adityanath's parliamentary stronghold for five consecutive terms.The defeat demonstrated that the BJP's support among non-Yadav OBC communities could be disrupted when Nishad mobilisation combined with the SP's wider social coalition.But the equation soon changed again.Before the 2019 Lok Sabha election, the Nishad Party moved into the BJP-led NDA. Praveen Nishad joined the BJP and contested the Sant Kabir Nagar Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket, winning the election.The BJP-Nishad Party alliance became an important part of the BJP's strategy to consolidate non-Yadav OBC support in eastern Uttar Pradesh.
2019 and 2022: Alliance and the unfinished bargain
The BJP and Nishad Party continued their alliance into the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly election.The BJP won 255 seats, while the Nishad Party won six. The NDA retained power with 273 seats in the 403-member assembly.For the BJP, the alliance helped reinforce its eastern Uttar Pradesh coalition.For Sanjay Nishad, however, being part of the government brought a different problem: once an ally enters government, its demands are increasingly judged against what it can actually secure from that government.The biggest unresolved issue remained the demand for Scheduled Caste status for sections of the Nishad community.Sanjay Nishad has repeatedly pressed the BJP government on the demand.On August 18, 2026, just months before the 2027 elections, he escalated the issue again, saying he was prepared to give up his ministerial position if necessary.His friction with the BJP had also become visible after the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when he blamed BJP leaders for his son Praveen Nishad's defeat in Sant Kabir Nagar.Praveen, who contested the seat on a BJP ticket, lost to the Samajwadi Party's Laxmikant Pappu Nishad.The result was another reminder that a BJP-Nishad Party alliance does not necessarily translate into a uniform Nishad vote.
SP and Congress try to prise open BJP's base
That fluidity is what the opposition is trying to exploit ahead of 2027.In March 2026, it appointed Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti as chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Backward Classes Commission. The move came alongside the BJP's continuing alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP responded by appointing Phoolan Devi's sister, 67-year-old Rukmini Devi, as president of the party's Uttar Pradesh women's wing. The appointment was seen as part of Akhilesh Yadav's PDA — Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — outreach ahead of the 2027 election.Rukmini Devi subsequently attacked Sanjay Nishad, questioning what he had delivered for the community while being part of the government.The appointments show that the competition for the Nishad vote is not merely about alliances. It is a contest over who represents the community's political memory.Congress, on the other hand, has a more difficult task because its organisational presence among Nishads is weaker.Its August outreach in Tarun was therefore significant. Ajay Rai's visit to the Nishad community programme was an attempt to establish a direct connection with the community.The party's subsequent defence of the event, that the hosts were Nishads with their own food traditions, also allowed Congress to frame the controversy around community identity and traditional livelihoods rather than solely religious conduct.For the SP and Congress, the broader argument is that the Nishad vote is not synonymous with the Nishad Party.
The VIP factor
The Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP), led by Bihar-based Nishad leader Mukesh Sahani, adds another layer to this contest.VIP entered Uttar Pradesh politics in the 2022 assembly election, seeking support among Nishads and other Extremely Backward Classes, particularly in Purvanchal.The party did not emerge as a major electoral force, but its campaign showed how smaller caste-based parties can complicate a close contest.VIP contested more than 100 seats, primarily in eastern Uttar Pradesh, and said its candidates polled more votes than Congress candidates in 15 constituencies, including Bairia, Bansdih, Phephna, Alapur, Jalalpur, Ghanghata, Balha, Shahganj and Kerakat.Its relationship with the BJP has been politically fluid rather than a straightforward alliance in Uttar Pradesh.Sahani has been a vocal critic of the BJP at various points. However, in neighbouring Bihar where the Nishads remain relevant across the seats in the Ganga area, his political trajectory has repeatedly shifted. VIP contested as part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, switched to the NDA for the 2020 Bihar assembly election (winning 4 seats and entering the cabinet), but was dropped from the NDA in 2022 after contesting against the BJP in UP. In last year's Bihar polls, his party failed to secure any seat.However, in upcoming polls in UP, a few thousand votes in its favour can alter the results in close constituencies.
The 2027 question
The fish controversy may fade, but the political question it has exposed is unlikely to disappear.The BJP has the advantage of a long association with the Ram movement, an established organisational network and an alliance with the Nishad Party.
The SP is seeking to revive the community's social-justice connection through Phoolan Devi's political legacy and the PDA framework.Congress is attempting to build a direct relationship with Nishad voters, while smaller parties such as VIP can potentially fragment the vote.For the Nishads themselves, however, the choice is unlikely to be framed around a single issue.Their political history has moved from the epic memory of Nishadraj and Ekalavya, to participation in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, to the social-justice politics associated with Phoolan Devi, to the rise of the Nishad Party, its alliance with the BJP and subsequent friction over representation and reservation.The lesson from that history is clear: the Nishad vote has never been permanently owned by one party.In 2027, the contest will be over whether Ram and the BJP's organisational alliance can outweigh demands for reservation, representation and livelihoods - and whether the opposition can convert those demands into votes.
